test_plan.title: Manual Update of User Responses for Notifications
test_plan.steps:
- Log in as a Notification Manager and navigate to a "response required" notification with at least one user having "pending" status; click the pencil edit icon on that user's row, select a response value from the dropdown, save, and verify the status updates immediately with an info icon and audit trail recorded.
- Verify that a previously manually updated response cannot be overwritten by a subsequent text reply from the user by having a user send a text response after a manager has set their status; confirm the manually entered value persists.
- Log in as a non-Manager user (Supervisor or other role), navigate to the notification responses tracking page, and confirm the pencil edit icon is not visible on any response rows and the page is read-only.
- Download the CSV export for a notification containing manually updated responses and verify the "Manually Updated By" column captures the manager's name/ID for each manually modified row.
- As a Notification Manager, click the pencil icon on a response row, modify the value to a different option, save, and verify the historical log retains the previous response while the current value and timestamp reflect the new update.

test_plan.title: Fix supervisor reminder email — NullReferenceException on missing TimeZone.Name
test_plan.steps:
- Verify that the supervisor "did not report" email is successfully sent at the scheduled 9:30 AM trigger time, even when one or more employee records in the system have a WorkSite.TimeZone with a null Name value.
- Confirm that no NullReferenceException is logged in the application event log or worker service logs when the scheduled task executes.
- Check that supervisors receive the expected morning reminder email for employee who did not report, using test data that includes at least one employee record with a null TimeZone.Name.
- Verify that the fix does not prevent emails from being sent to supervisors of employee with valid (non-null) TimeZone.Name values.

test_plan.title: Fix mobile check-in: capture free-text note after menu option
test_plan.steps:
- Send a mobile check-in text with menu option 4 followed by free-text (e.g., `4 Going to meeting`)
- Verify the check-in note contains both the auto-generated message and the free-text note on separate lines
- Repeat with different menu options (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) each with trailing text to confirm free-text is captured for all options
- Send a check-in with menu option only (no trailing text) and verify only the auto-generated note appears without an empty "Note:" line
- Verify trimming works by sending menu option with leading/trailing whitespace in the free-text portion (e.g., `4   Going to meeting   `) and confirm extra spaces are removed

sprint_report.goals: This sprint aimed to stabilize the platform by addressing critical data integrity bugs in the Layer and Customer management workflows while laying the architectural groundwork for a multi-database CosmosDB migration. The team also standardized the user experience across administrative forms by implementing consistent navigation patterns.
sprint_report.summary: The sprint delivered fixes to several high-impact production issues, including resolving orphaned CustomerLayer references when renaming layers, correcting the supervisor reminder email null reference error, and fixing mobile check-in note capture. In parallel, the team completed the migration strategy and database schema work for CosmosDB, establishing separate tenant, geo, system, lookup, and identity databases to support better scaling and data isolation. Across the administrative interface, the team systematized the user experience by adding Cancel buttons and confirmation modals to 47 forms, improving data safety and navigation consistency. These efforts collectively reduce support burden from data corruption issues, enable the upcoming database migration, and create a more predictable administrative experience for customers and internal staff.
